setlist.title: Goin' Down The Road Feeling Bad

liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **Feel Like A Stranger** (1 review): Transition to Terrapin is unique, skipping the usual three-beat rhythm for an effortless ease [19]
- **Goin' Down The Road Feeling Bad** (1 review): The performance of Goin' Down The Road Feeling Bad is described as absolutely manic [24]

## The recordings

- **gd1980-05-11.mtx.dusborne.126880.flac16** (recommended): matrix (soundboard mixed with audience mics); 23 songs; 164 min; rated 4.25/5 by 4 [1]. Said about its sound: Matrix combines board and audience sources, highlighting Jerry's wah-wah solo at the end of Fire; Matrix offers clarity and crowd energy, with excellent leads on Don't Ease Me In [24][25]
- **gd1980-05-11.nak300.friend.andrewf.107227.flac16**: matrix (soundboard mixed with audience mics); 23 songs; 158 min; rated 4/5 by 1 [2]. Said about its sound: Audience recording has more definition and less reverb than the SBD or matrix [28]
- **gd1980-05-11.sbd.miller.89577.sbeok.flac16**: soundboard; 23 songs; 156 min; rated 3.25/5 by 4 [3]. Said about its sound: Hiss is present but fades during the intense jamming of the second set; Hiss was from the hall PA, masked by the band's loud volume [18][26]
- **gd1980-05-11.sbd.terrapinstation.tetzeli.fix-12259.33501.reflac.flac16**: soundboard; 23 songs; 158 min [4]
- **gd1980-05-11.fob.glassberg.motb-0052.97522.flac16**: source not stated; 23 songs; 162 min; rated 5/5 by 4 [6]. Said about its sound: Left microphone was slightly obstructed, creating a muted sound on this song [6]
- **gd1980-05-11.aud.willy.7539.sbeok.shnf**: audience recording; 23 songs; 155 min; rated 4.5/5 by 2 [12]. Said about its sound: Jerry's amplified voice has a growl, and the crowd clapping is notably tight [17]

## Around the show

- Listener recalls moving to Portland and attending shows from their apartment in bare feet [17]
- The show was a nice Mother's Day performance with a very nice first set [19]
- Listener traveled from Orono, meeting friends at Front Street Station seats [22]
- Crowd was tight with the band, and some really good weed was going around [22]
- The atmosphere was hot and sultry with lots of X Factor energy [28]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd1980-05-11.mtx.dusborne.126880.flac16**: transferred by Matrix by Dave Usborne; source: 2 Source Matrix By Dave Usborne;soundboard (shnid:89577); Transfers and Mastering By Charlie Miller;Recording Info:SBD -> Cassette Master -> Cassette -> Dat ->… [1]
- **gd1980-05-11.nak300.friend.andrewf.107227.flac16**: taped by Tim Friend; transferred by Andrew F.; source: 2x Nakamichi CM300/CP1's > Sony TC-153SD > Maxell XLII's. Mics on stand "next to the soundboard". [2]
- **gd1980-05-11.sbd.miller.89577.sbeok.flac16**: transferred by Charlie Miller; source: SBD -> Cassette Master -> Cassette -> Dat -> CD [3]. Also: SBD patch source recorded by Steve Rolfe, with channels swapped and fixed; Repitch correction of plus 1.2 percent applied to the soundboard recording [3]
- **gd1980-05-11.sbd.terrapinstation.tetzeli.fix-12259.33501.reflac.flac16**: transferred by Bill Tetzeli; source: SHN (12259) -> wav (CE Pro) -> flac (Trader's Little Helper) [4]. Also: Patches made using Rolfe, Pujol, and Vernon audience source downloaded from archive.org [4]
- **gd1980-05-11.fob.glassberg.motb-0052.97522.flac16**: taped by Barry Glassberg; transferred by Adam Egert; source: FOB: 2 x Nakamichi CM700 => Sony TC-D5 >> MAC [6]
- **gd1980-05-11.aud.willy.7539.sbeok.shnf**: taped by Frank Venezia; transferred by Frank Venezia; source: Nak 300's>Sony D5>master cassette [12]
